prompt: Single continuous cinematic shot, no scene cuts. A dim home office at 3 a.m. A developer is asleep face-down on the desk next to a laptop. On the laptop screen, large green text reads: 16 / 16 PASS. Through the window behind, the sky slowly turns from black to pale dawn blue over 8 seconds. A desk lamp, cold coffee, a drone propeller on the desk. Sound: a quiet laptop fan, one soft notification chime at 6 seconds. No dialogue, no music.

Single continuous cinematic shot, no scene cuts. A small quadcopter drone hovers in a bright white tiled test room with orange gate frames. A thin red laser grid sweeps out from the drone across the floor and walls like a scanner; the grid freezes on one spot and a glowing red lock-on reticle snaps onto it, with a sharp tick. Then the drone's lights flick from red to calm blue and it flies off through the first gate. Sound: scanner hum, a sharp lock tone, rotors. No dialogue, no music, no readable text.

Single continuous shot, no scene cuts. A long bright white room with sixteen identical small white toy robots sitting in a row at sixteen tiny desks, each with a yellow sticky note stuck to its chest, all typing in perfect unison at tiny keyboards. The camera dollies slowly along the row. Playful and slightly unsettling. Sound: sixteen tiny keyboards clicking in sync. No dialogue, no music, no readable text.

Single continuous cinematic shot, no scene cuts. A stern referee in a black and white striped shirt stands at the edge of a bright white tiled drone test room holding a clipboard and a stopwatch. A small gray quadcopter drone comes through an orange gate frame, slows, and settles gently onto a round green landing pad marked LAND. The referee clicks the stopwatch, looks at the clipboard, and gives a single slow nod. Deadpan comedy. Sound: rotors winding down, the stopwatch click. No dialogue, no music.

Single continuous cinematic shot, no scene cuts. Golden dawn light floods an empty warehouse through tall windows. A small quadcopter drone descends slowly and lands perfectly on a round green pad. As it settles, large clean white title text fades in over the scene reading exactly: DID IT LEARN? and below it smaller text: github.com/carrollco/did-it-learn. Hold on the title. Sound: rotors winding down, soft wind, a single warm low piano note. No dialogue.
